title: Survey the sterile-neutrino short-baseline anomaly status…

turns.text: Survey the sterile-neutrino short-baseline anomaly status (2024-2026) and contrast with BBN/CMB N_eff limits (use the BBN tools for numbers). Are eV-scale sterile neutrinos still viable?

**Survey.** The team found 32 tools on 3 servers and 1 relevant paper, and ran 6 read-only probes.

By 2024-2026 the simple 3+1 eV sterile neutrino explanation of short-baseline anomalies is strongly disfavored. MicroBooNE LArTPC data in two beams (2024-2025) excludes the LSND/MiniBooNE appearance interpretation at 95% CL, and the STEREO final 119-day dataset (Dec 2024) plus PROSPECT+STEREO combined analyses exclude the canonical reactor-antineutrino-anomaly parameter space at >99.9% CL, attributing the 6% rate deficit and shape anomaly to flux-prediction biases. The gallium anomaly (SAGE/GALLEX/BEST >5 sigma) persists, with 2025-2026 re-analyses still finding a deficit consistent with Delta m^2 ~1 eV^2, sin^2 2theta ~0.4, but in strong tension with reactor and accelerator nulls and global 3+1 fits. Cosmology (Planck + ACT + DESI BAO 2024-2025) constrains N_eff = 2.99 +/- 0.17 and sum m_nu, so a fully thermalized eV sterile with Delta N_eff ~1 is excluded at high significance unless thermalization is suppressed by large lepton asymmetry, secret interactions, low reheating temperature or other non-standard cosmology.

The plan should check:
- N_eff total and Delta N_eff from sterile thermalization vs Planck+ACT+DESI limit N_eff = 2.99 +/- 0.17 (SM 3.044).
- Primordial helium-4 mass fraction Yp vs BBN prediction as function of Delta N_eff.
- Deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio D/H vs BBN prediction as function of Delta N_eff and baryon density.
- Sterile parameters m_s, Delta m^2_41 ~1 eV^2 and sin^2 2theta ~0.01-0.5 for SBL preferred regions (LSND/MiniBooNE, BEST, reactor).
- Thermalization fraction and relic density Omega_s h^2 / effective mass m_eff constrained by CMB+LSS free-streaming.
- X-ray decay line energy E = m_s/2 and mixing limit to contrast eV SBL scale with keV dark-matter scale.

**Plan.** Three lines of investigation.

1. Quantitative BBN/CMB N_eff exclusion for eV sterile neutrinos - direct numbers for canonical SBL best-fit and grid. Core of viability question is Delta N_eff from thermalization vs Planck+ACT+DESI N_eff=2.99+/-0.17 (SM 3.044) and BBN Yp/D/H. Provides reproducible numbers to contrast with SBL claims.
2. Literature survey of SBL anomaly status 2024-2026: MicroBooNE, STEREO, PROSPECT, BEST/gallium, reactor flux re-evaluation, global 3+1 fits. Task requires grounding in 2024-2026 results that disfavor simple 3+1: MicroBooNE LArTPC two-beam 95% CL exclusion, STEREO final 119-day Dec 2024 and PROSPECT+STEREO >99.9% CL exclusion of reactor anomaly, persistent gallium >5 sigma but tension with nulls, and cosmology N_eff limits.
3. Thermalization threshold, exclusion plane overlay, and viability assessment with non-standard loopholes and eV vs keV contrast. Go beyond direct exclusion to show why eV sterile is excluded in standard cosmology (thermalization for sin^2 2theta >~1e-3) and what non-standard suppression (large lepton asymmetry, secret interactions, low reheating) would be required, plus contrast eV SBL scale with keV dark-matter X-ray scale.

The critic asked for changes:
- Tool budget exceeded: 1 describe +1 check +3-5 predict +1 grid +1 scan +1 plot_bbn_impact +1 compute_statistics +1 set_dispatch = 10-12 calls. Limit predict_sterile_nu to 2-3 anchors, drop compute_statistics/set_dispatch (dispatch is local per probe), and choose either grid OR scan for initial mapping to stay <=10.
- Missing robustness: must document standard-cosmology assumption (zero lepton asymmetry, no secret interactions) from describe_sterile_nu_tools and compare Yp/D/H to observed values with errors, not only N_eff sigma = (N_eff_pred-2.99)/0.17. Otherwise Delta N_eff~1 and >5 sigma claims are unverifiable.
- Tool budget exceeded: 2-3 web_search +4-6 read_arxiv_chunk +5 cite +2-4 get_paper_figures = 13-17 calls. Prioritize 3-4 key papers (STEREO final Dec 2024, PROSPECT+STEREO combined, MicroBooNE 2024-2025, BEST/gallium) plus arXiv:2504.16590, and cap figure extraction to 1-2.

**Wave 1.** Three directions run in parallel.
- Quantitative BBN/CMB N_eff exclusion for eV sterile neutrinos - direct numbers for canonical SBL best-fit and grid.
- Literature survey of SBL anomaly status 2024-2026: MicroBooNE, STEREO, PROSPECT, BEST/gallium, reactor flux re-evaluation, global 3+1 fits.
- Thermalization threshold, exclusion plane overlay, and viability assessment with non-standard loopholes and eV vs keV contrast.

**Completed — Quantitative BBN/CMB N_eff exclusion for eV sterile neutrinos - direct numbers for canonical SBL best-fit and grid.** Direction d-01 established quantitative BBN/CMB N_eff exclusion for eV sterile neutrinos in standard cosmology (Dodelson-Widrow production, no lepton asymmetry). Canonical SBL best-fit (Delta m^2=1.3 eV^2, m_s=1.14 eV, sin^2 2theta=0.42) fully thermalizes to Delta N_eff=1.0, N_eff total 4.044, excluded at 6.2 sigma vs Planck+ACT+DESI N_eff=2.99±0.17 (SM 3.044) and Delta chi^2_BBN=23.1 vs SM (threshold 3.84 at 95%), with Yp=0.2596 vs observed 0.2449±0.004 and D/H=2.777e-5 vs 2.547±0.025e-5, Omega_s h^2=29.3 vs observed DM 0.12. Grid m_s=0.1-10 eV, sin^2 2theta=1e-4 to 1 (49 points, file sterile_nu_grid_DW_1ddeb2.csv) shows Delta N_eff=1.0 for all sin^2 2theta>=0.01 at any eV mass, 37/49 BBN-excluded, threshold at 1e-4 gives 0.04 allowed and 1e-3 gives 0.40 marginal (Delta chi^2=0.62, 2.7 sigma vs Planck). Anchor points: BEST-like 1 eV 0.4 gives N_eff=4.044 Omega=22.0 excluded; reactor-like 0.09 same N_eff Omega=4.96 excluded; low-mixing 1e-3 gives N_eff=3.44 Omega=0.055 allowed; keV contrast 7100 eV 7e-11 gives Delta N_eff=0.00043 N_eff=3.044 Omega=0.033 allowed. Full scan 0.1-10 eV 3600 points (scan_DW_9bdb63.csv/.npz) finds 2597/3600 BBN-excluded and 2362/3600 overclosing, BBN-allowed max sin^2 2theta=0.00122. BBN impact plot Figure 1 bbn_vs_neff.png quantifies SM Yp=0.2468 D/H=2.443e-5 vs N_eff=4.044 Yp=0.2596 D/H=2.777e-5 (3.7 sigma in Yp), slopes dYp/dN_eff=0.0135 and dD/H/dN_eff=0.331e-5, BBN alone limits Delta N_eff<0.55 at 95%. Caveat: partial thermalization uses crude fit, full QKE gives Delta N_eff=0.93 at 1e-3 where fit gives 0.40, so limits are conservative. Remaining: exclusion plane overlay plot not generated, compute_statistics not run, non-standard loopholes not quantified.

**Blocked — Thermalization threshold, exclusion plane overlay, and viability assessment with non-standard loopholes and eV vs keV contrast.** Tool budget (10 calls) exhausted after core grid/scan/X-ray/BEST checks and exclusion plot; SBL contour digitization/overlay and literature search for loophole mechanisms could not run. DNS failure on web_search also blocked non-standard mechanism survey. Direction d-03 established quantitative thermalization and exclusion results for eV sterile neutrinos in standard Dodelson-Widrow cosmology; SBL contour overlay and non-standard loophole literature remain open due to tool budget exhaustion. What was done (all local execution): - Thermalization threshold grid: 27 points (m_s=0.5,1,3 eV x sin^2 2theta=1e-4 to 1) shows sharp transition. For all three eV masses, sin^2 2theta=1e-3 gives Delta N_eff=0.40 (Delta chi2 BBN=0.62, allowed), sin^2 2theta=3e-3 gives Delta N_eff=1.0 (Delta chi2=23.1, excluded at 95% CL). Threshold for near-complete thermalization is sin^2 2theta ~1-3e-3. File: sterile_nu_grid_DW_b2a7f6.csv. - BBN/relic-density exclusion plane scan: 3600 points (m_s 0.1-10 eV, sin^2 2theta 1e-4 to 1, DW). 2597/3600 BBN-excluded (Delta chi2>3.84) and 2362/3600 overclose (Omega_s h2>0.12). Maximum BBN-allowed mixing is sin^2 2theta=0.00122 at all sampled eV masses. Files: scan_DW_9bdb63.csv and .npz. - Canonical BEST SBL best-fit (m_s=1.14 eV, Delta m2=1.3 eV2, sin^2 2theta=0.42) predicts Delta N_eff=1.0 (N_eff=4.044), Omega_s h2=29.3 (244x observed DM 0.12), BBN Yp=0.2596 (obs 0.2449+/-0.004) and D/H=2.78e-5 (obs 2.547+/-0.025e-5) with Delta chi2=23.1 vs SM, 6.2 sigma tension with Planck N_eff=2.99+/-0.17 (33 sigma for CMB-S4 sigma=0.03). - eV vs keV contrast: keV benchmark m_s=7.1 keV, sin^2 2theta=7e-11 gives E_gamma=m_s/2=3.55 keV, lifetime 5.8e27 s (1.8e20 yr), excluded by NuSTAR M31 and XMM-Newton blank sky. eV SBL mixing 0.1-0.5 is 9-10 orders of magnitude larger than keV DM mixing 2e-11 to 2e-10; eV decay photons at 0.00057 keV are unobservable vs keV X-ray line. - Exclusion plane figure produced: Figure 2 (exclusion_scan_DW_9bdb63.png) from 3600-point scan showing BBN-excluded and overclosure regions with Omega_DM line and X-ray/Lyman-alpha limits. What was not done: - SBL preferred contour overlay (LSND/MiniBooNE, BEST, reactor) digitized from literature onto exclusion plane - requires get_paper_figures and manual digitization, not executed before budget limit. - Non-standard suppression literature search (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2, secret interactions, low reheating) - web_search failed with DNS error and budget exhausted. - Formatted thermalization scan plot and X-ray contrast table as publication-ready figures - numbers established but not plotted. **Blocked — Quantify non-standard loopholes required to reconcile eV sterile with N_eff=2.99+/-0.17 and their independent constraints.** Tool budget exhausted after 4 web_search + 2 predict_sterile_nu calls; no read_arxiv_chunk/cite calls available to extract verbatim quotes and arXiv IDs for loophole papers. Quantitative per-mechanism constraints remain open. Direction d-06 asked what non-standard physics would be needed to save an eV sterile neutrino (a fourth neutrino with mass ~1 eV) given the cosmological limit on extra radiation. The answer is that standard cosmology excludes it, and any loophole must suppress its contribution by more than a factor of three and is itself constrained. What was established: - The cosmological limit is N_eff (effective number of relativistic species, where the Standard Model predicts 3.044) = 2.99 +/- 0.17 from Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO. This implies Delta N_eff (extra radiation beyond the Standard Model) < 0.28 at 95% confidence (Gaussian 1.96 sigma upper limit on observed Delta = -0.054 +/- 0.17). A fully thermalized eV sterile contributes Delta N_eff = 1.0, so it must be suppressed by a factor >3.6 (1.0/0.28) to survive. - Two anchor points were computed locally with predict_sterile_nu (Dodelson-Widrow production, no lepton asymmetry): the canonical BEST short-baseline best fit (m_s = 1.14 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.42, where sin^2 2theta measures mixing with active neutrinos) gives Delta N_eff = 1.0, total N_eff = 4.044, relic density Omega_s h^2 = 29.3 (244 times the observed dark matter 0.12), BBN helium mass fraction Yp = 0.2596 versus observed 0.2449 +/- 0.004 and deuterium D/H = 2.78e-5 versus 2.547 +/- 0.025e-5, Delta chi^2_BBN = 23.1 versus Standard Model (threshold 3.84 at 95%), excluded at 6.2 sigma versus Planck. A low-mixing threshold point (m_s = 1.0 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.001) gives Delta N_eff = 0.40, N_eff = 3.44, Omega_s h^2 = 0.055, Delta chi^2 = 0.62 (allowed by BBN but still above the 0.28 CMB limit, 2.7 sigma tension). - Three classes of loopholes were identified from four web_search calls (2024-2026 literature snippets): large lepton asymmetry (primordial neutrino-antineutrino asymmetry L ~ 1e-2, especially flavor-asymmetric with near-zero total asymmetry that can evade BBN/CMB via oscillation equilibration), secret neutrino self-interactions (new interactions that generate finite-temperature suppression of active-sterile mixing), and low reheating temperature (reheating after inflation below the sterile production peak, so thermalization never completes). Each can in principle reduce Delta N_eff from 1.0 to <0.28 but is independently limited by BBN Yp/D/H, CMB free-streaming, structure formation, and collider constraints. - Viability statement: eV 3+1 sterile neutrinos are excluded in standard cosmology; they remain viable only with non-standard suppression that is itself constrained and requires tuned parameters. What ran and where: describe_sterile_nu_tools and two predict_sterile_nu evaluations ran locally; four web_search queries ran for literature leads. Existing artifacts were reused from /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_171616/ including bbn_vs_neff.png (Figure 1, Yp and D/H versus N_eff) and exclusion_scan_DW_9bdb63.png (Figure 2, 3600-point exclusion plane) and scan_DW_9bdb63.csv/.npz. What was not done: No read_arxiv_chunk or cite calls executed due to tool budget exhaustion (0 calls remaining), so the required 2-3 verbatim citations with arXiv IDs/DOIs and per-loophole quantitative limits (required L values, coupling strengths, T_RH thresholds) could not be provided. Web search snippets are not citable sources.

Web search established the qualitative status but tool budget prevented read_arxiv_chunk, cite, and get_paper_figures. STEREO final 119 reactor-on days (Oct 2017-Nov 2020, 107,588 antineutrinos at 2.5-7 m from ILL highly enriched uranium reactor) shows no distance over energy oscillation and excludes the canonical reactor anomaly eV sterile region at greater than 99.9 percent confidence level. MicroBooNE 170-ton liquid argon time projection chamber on the Booster beam saw no electron neutrino excess 2021-2024; June 2024 combined analysis excluded the MiniBooNE electron neutrino interpretation at greater than 99 percent confidence level and December 2025 two-beam data exclude the single light sterile LSND/MiniBooNE interpretation at 95 percent confidence level. PROSPECT (segmented detector about 7 m from High Flux Isotope Reactor) plus STEREO combined spectra are compatible with chi-squared over degrees of freedom 24.1 over 21 and exclude most reactor anomaly space; the 5 to 6 percent rate deficit and 5 MeV bump are attributed to flux prediction biases. Gallium anomaly (GALLEX/SAGE chromium-51 calibration) confirmed by BEST at greater than 5 sigma, consistent with mass splitting about 1 eV squared and mixing about 0.4, but in tension with reactor and accelerator nulls; arXiv:2504.16590 proposes an independent test using the same chromium-51 source via electron neutrino scattering. No .bib file with verbatim quotes was created and no figures with captions were saved in this direction. turns.report:
# eV-Scale Sterile Neutrinos Confront BBN and CMB $N_{\rm eff}$ Limits: Status of Short-Baseline Anomalies 2024-2026

## Abstract
The question was whether eV-scale sterile neutrinos that explain short-baseline anomalies remain viable against Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN, light-element formation in the early universe) and cosmic microwave background (CMB, relic radiation from recombination) limits on extra radiation. In standard cosmology with Dodelson-Widrow production (collision-driven thermalization with no lepton asymmetry) the canonical short-baseline best fit at $m_s = 1.14\,\mathrm{eV}$, $\Delta m^2_{41} = 1.3\,\mathrm{eV}^2$, $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.42$ fully thermalizes to $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 1.0$ and $N_{\rm eff} = 4.044$, excluded at $6.2\sigma$ versus Planck 2018 $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99 \pm 0.17$ and at $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} = 23.1$ versus the Standard Model. All short-baseline preferred mixings lie 8 to 400 times above the BBN-allowed maximum of $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.00122$. The gallium anomaly persists but its sterile interpretation is in strong tension with reactor and accelerator nulls, and no non-standard loophole was quantified with citable sources in this run.

## Background
Sterile neutrinos are hypothetical neutral fermions that mix with active neutrinos but feel no weak interactions. A fourth mass state with $m_s \sim 1\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\Delta m^2_{41} \sim 1\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ was invoked to explain several short-baseline anomalies. The effective number of relativistic species $N_{\rm eff}$ (radiation density in neutrino-like units, Standard Model $N_{\rm eff} = 3.044$) and BBN yields of helium-4 mass fraction $Y_p$ and deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio $D/H$ constrain any extra thermalized species. The literature surveyed by web search (not independently verified with verbatim citations in this run) reports that by 2024-2026 the simple 3+1 (three active plus one sterile) eV explanation is strongly disfavored, while the gallium anomaly remains. One key paper identified is arXiv:2504.16590 Testing the Gallium anomaly using Electron-Neutrino Scattering, which proposes an independent test of the gallium deficit using the same chromium-51 source but detecting neutrinos via electron-neutrino scattering rather than capture.

Cosmology from Planck 2018 temperature, polarization, low-multipole and lensing plus baryon acoustic oscillations gives $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99 \pm 0.17$, consistent with $3.044$. BBN observations used here are $Y_p = 0.2449 \pm 0.004$ and $D/H = 2.547 \pm 0.025 \times 10^{-5}$. No Planck+ACT+DESI BAO 2024-2025 update beyond Planck 2018 was executed in this run due to tool budget exhaustion and DNS failures.

## Results

All quantitative BBN and $N_{\rm eff}$ calculations ran locally via the sterile-neutrino BBN server and are saved in `/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_171616/`. No high-performance computing facility was used. The BBN fit is PRyMordial-calibrated with $<0.3\%$ accuracy, valid for $N_{\rm eff} = 2.044$ to $6.044$, $\omega_b h^2 = 0.019$ to $0.0257$, neutron lifetime $\tau_n = 866.4$ to $890.4\,\mathrm{s}$, and $m_s \lesssim 100\,\mathrm{keV}$ where the sterile is relativistic at BBN. Exclusion uses $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} > 3.84$ at $95\%$ confidence for one degree of freedom versus the Standard Model. Standard cosmology assumes zero lepton asymmetry (matter-antimatter imbalance in leptons) and no secret interactions.

### Canonical short-baseline best fit versus BBN and CMB
The canonical BEST-motivated point at $m_s = 1.14\,\mathrm{eV}$, $\Delta m^2_{41} = 1.3\,\mathrm{eV}^2$, $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.42$ (where $\sin^2 2\theta$ measures active-sterile mixing) fully thermalizes in standard Dodelson-Widrow cosmology to $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 1.0$ and $N_{\rm eff} = 4.044$. This predicts $Y_p = 0.2596$ versus observed $Y_p = 0.2449 \pm 0.004$ and $D/H = 2.777 \times 10^{-5}$ versus $2.547 \pm 0.025 \times 10^{-5}$, with combined $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} = 23.1$ (threshold $3.84$). The relic density is $\Omega_s h^2 = 29.3$ versus observed dark matter $\Omega_{\rm DM} h^2 = 0.12 \pm 0.001$, a factor of 244 too high. Versus Planck 2018 $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99 \pm 0.17$ the tension is $6.2\sigma$, and would be $33\sigma$ for a future CMB-S4 uncertainty of $0.03$. The $95\%$ limit from Planck 2018 is $\Delta N_{\rm eff} < 0.28$ (observed $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = -0.054 \pm 0.17$, upper limit $-0.054 + 1.96 \times 0.17 = 0.28$), so a fully thermalized sterile requires suppression by more than $3.6$ to survive.

### Grid scans and thermalization threshold
A 49-point product grid at $m_s = 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 1.14, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\sin^2 2\theta = 10^{-4}$ to $1$ shows near-complete thermalization with $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 1.0$ for all $\sin^2 2\theta \ge 0.01$ at any eV mass. In that grid $37/49$ points are BBN-excluded and $36/49$ overclose with $\Omega_s h^2 > 0.12$. At $\sin^2 2\theta = 10^{-4}$ the model gives $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 0.04$ and is allowed, while at $\sin^2 2\theta = 10^{-3}$ it gives $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 0.40$ with $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} = 0.62$ (marginally allowed by BBN but $2.7\sigma$ high versus Planck).

- Recompute the thermalization threshold with full quantum kinetic equations to propagate the $1$ to $3 \times 10^{-3}$ uncertainty to exclusion fractions and the maximum allowed mixing.

BBN observations $Y_p = 0.2449 \pm 0.004$ and $D/H = 2.547 \pm 0.025 \times 10^{-5}$ provide complementary limits via $Y_p$ and $D/H$ versus $N_{\rm eff}$.

The sterile-neutrino BBN server validity was documented as PRyMordial-calibrated, valid for $N_{\rm eff} = 2.044$ to $6.044$, $\omega_b h^2 = 0.019$ to $0.0257$, $\tau_n = 866.4$ to $890.4\,\mathrm{s}$, and $m_s \lesssim 100\,\mathrm{keV}$ where the sterile is relativistic at BBN. Exclusion uses $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} > 3.84$ at $95\%$ CL for one degree of freedom versus the Standard Model, under standard cosmology with zero lepton asymmetry and no secret interactions. Existing artifacts were verified in `runs/261107_171616/` as `scan_DW_9bdb63.csv` and `scan_DW_9bdb63.npz` (3600 points), `sterile_nu_grid_DW_1ddeb2.csv` (49 points), `sterile_nu_grid_DW_b2a7f6.csv` (27-point threshold grid), `bbn_vs_neff.png` (Figure 1) and `exclusion_scan_DW_9bdb63.png` (Figure 2).

## Discussion
In standard cosmology eV-scale sterile neutrinos with mixings required by short-baseline anomalies are excluded by both BBN and CMB $N_{\rm eff}$. The canonical BEST point at $m_s = 1.14\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.42$ predicts $N_{\rm eff} = 4.044$, $Y_p = 0.2596$ and $D/H = 2.78 \times 10^{-5}$ with $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} = 23.1$, and $\Omega_s h^2 = 29.3$, all far from observed values. The 3600-point scan shows $72\%$ BBN-excluded and $66\%$ overclosing, with a maximum allowed mixing of $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.00122$, well below all short-baseline preferred regions at $0.01$ to $0.5$. Even the low-mixing threshold at $\sin^2 2\theta = 0.001$ with $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 0.40$ and $N_{\rm eff} = 3.44$ exceeds the Planck 2018 $95\%$ limit of $\Delta N_{\rm eff} < 0.28$ by $2.7\sigma$, while BBN alone allows it with $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} = 0.62$.

This agrees with the literature trend reported in web snippets that MicroBooNE and STEREO see no oscillation and that the reactor rate and shape anomalies are attributed to flux-prediction biases, but those experimental claims were not independently verified here and remain contested. The gallium anomaly persistence is also reported but its sterile interpretation is in tension with nulls, and the proposed electron-scattering test in arXiv:2504.16590 has not been executed as a re-analysis in this run.

Three non-standard loopholes were identified from snippets as capable in principle of suppressing $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ from $1.0$ to $<0.28$: large lepton asymmetry $L \sim 10^{-2}$ especially flavor-asymmetric with near-zero total asymmetry washed out by oscillations at MeV temperatures, secret neutrino self-interactions that generate a finite-temperature matter potential suppressing active-sterile mixing, and low reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH} \ll 100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ where production never completes. Each is independently constrained by BBN $Y_p$ and $D/H$, CMB free-streaming, large-scale structure and laboratory bounds, but no per-loophole quantitative limits with verbatim citations were obtained.

Dead ends encountered were DNS resolution failures for web searches, tool budget exhaustion after 6 web searches blocking `read_arxiv_chunk`, `cite` and `get_paper_figures` so no .bib with 5 verbatim quotes including arXiv:2504.16590 and no 1 to 2 extracted figures were produced, failure to digitize LSND, MiniBooNE, BEST and reactor preferred contours onto the exclusion plane, failure of `compute_statistics` via `load_table_data` which only searches the input directory not the runs directory (verified instead by direct file reads), and use of a crude Dodelson-Widrow fit that underestimates $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ at $\sin^2 2\theta = 10^{-3}$ ($0.40$ versus $0.93$ from full quantum kinetic equations), making limits conservative.

## Limitations
What could not be established and why:

- No literature survey with 5 verbatim citations including arXiv:2504.16590 and no extracted published figures with captions were delivered, because the tool budget was exhausted after web searches and DNS failures blocked `read_arxiv_chunk`, `cite` and `get_paper_figures`. All 2024-2026 short-baseline claims therefore rely on uncitable snippets.
- No Planck+ACT+DESI BAO 2024-2025 $N_{\rm eff}$ update beyond Planck 2018 $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99 \pm 0.17$ was executed for the same budget and DNS reasons.
- No quantitative per-loophole requirements for lepton asymmetry, secret-interaction coupling strength or $T_{\rm RH}$ thresholds and their independent constraints were established, because citable sources could not be retrieved.
- No SBL preferred contour overlay on the exclusion plane was generated, because literature figures were not extracted and manual digitization was not executed before budget limit.
- No `compute_statistics` percentiles were run via the server tool due to input-directory restriction; statistics were verified by direct CSV reads.
- BBN limits rely on a PRyMordial-calibrated fit valid only for $m_s \lesssim 100\,\mathrm{keV}$ and standard cosmology; non-standard thermal histories were not modeled.

## Open directions
- Quantify the lepton asymmetry, secret-interaction coupling and reheating temperature needed to suppress a BEST-like sterile with $\sin^2 2\theta \sim 0.4$ from $\Delta N_{\rm eff} = 1.0$ to $<0.28$ and check each against BBN $Y_p$ and $D/H$ and CMB free-streaming limits.
- Complete the 2024-2026 literature survey with 5 verbatim citations including arXiv:2504.16590 and 1 to 2 extracted figures for STEREO final and MicroBooNE to verify $>99.9\%$ and $>99\%$ CL claims.
- Digitize LSND, MiniBooNE, BEST and reactor preferred contours from published figures and overlay them on the 3600-point BBN and overclosure exclusion plane.
- Perform a global 3+1 fit parameter goodness-of-fit test quantifying tension between gallium persistence and reactor plus accelerator nulls including the proposed electron-scattering test.
- Recompute the thermalization threshold with full quantum kinetic equations to propagate the $1$ to $3 \times 10^{-3}$ uncertainty to exclusion fractions and the maximum allowed mixing.

result.summary:
Direction d-06 asked what non-standard physics would be needed to save an eV sterile neutrino (a fourth neutrino with mass ~1 eV) given cosmological limits on extra radiation. Standard cosmology excludes it; any loophole must suppress its contribution by more than a factor of three and is itself constrained.

What was established:
- The cosmological limit is N_eff (effective number of relativistic species, Standard Model predicts 3.044) = 2.99 +/- 0.17 from Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO. This implies Delta N_eff (extra radiation beyond Standard Model) < 0.28 at 95% confidence (Gaussian 1.96 sigma upper limit on observed Delta = -0.054 +/- 0.17). A fully thermalized eV sterile contributes Delta N_eff = 1.0, so it must be suppressed by factor >3.6 (1.0/0.28) to survive.
- Two anchor points computed locally with predict_sterile_nu (Dodelson-Widrow production, no lepton asymmetry): canonical BEST short-baseline best fit (m_s = 1.14 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.42, where sin^2 2theta measures mixing with active neutrinos) gives Delta N_eff = 1.0, total N_eff = 4.044, relic density Omega_s h^2 = 29.3 (244 times observed dark matter 0.12), BBN helium mass fraction Yp = 0.2596 versus observed 0.2449 +/- 0.004 and deuterium D/H = 2.78e-5 versus 2.547 +/- 0.025e-5, Delta chi^2_BBN = 23.1 versus Standard Model (threshold 3.84 at 95%), excluded at 6.2 sigma versus Planck. Low-mixing threshold point (m_s = 1.0 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.001) gives Delta N_eff = 0.40, N_eff = 3.44, Omega_s h^2 = 0.055, Delta chi^2 = 0.62 (allowed by BBN but still above 0.28 CMB limit, 2.7 sigma tension).
- Three loophole classes identified from web_search literature leads (2024-2026 snippets, not citable): large lepton asymmetry L ~ 1e-2 (especially flavor-asymmetric with near-zero total asymmetry washed out by oscillations at MeV, evading BBN/CMB), secret neutrino self-interactions (finite-temperature suppression of active-sterile mixing), and low reheating temperature T_RH << 100 MeV (production never completes). Each can in principle reduce Delta N_eff from 1.0 to <0.28 but is independently limited by BBN Yp/D/H, CMB free-streaming, structure formation and laboratory bounds.
- Viability statement: eV 3+1 sterile neutrinos are excluded in standard cosmology; viable only with non-standard suppression that is itself constrained and requires tuned parameters.

What ran and where: describe_sterile_nu_tools and two predict_sterile_nu evaluations ran locally; four web_search queries ran for literature leads. Existing artifacts reused from /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_171616/ including bbn_vs_neff.png (Figure 1, Yp and D/H versus N_eff) and exclusion_scan_DW_9bdb63.png (Figure 2, 3600-point exclusion plane) and scan_DW_9bdb63.csv/.npz. No new output files were written in this direction.

What was not done and remains open: No read_arxiv_chunk or cite calls executed due to tool budget exhaustion, so required 2-3 verbatim citations with arXiv IDs/DOIs and per-loophole quantitative limits (required L values, coupling strengths, T_RH thresholds) could not be provided. Web search snippets are not citable sources. Recorded as dead end x-06.

brief.summary: The eV sterile neutrino interpretation of LSND (3.8 sigma) and MiniBooNE low-energy excess is in strong tension with cosmology: a fully thermalized eV sterile gives Delta N_eff ~1, excluded by Planck 2018 N_eff=2.99+/-0.17 and BBN Yp/D/H. MicroBooNE LAr data disfavors the simple nu_mu->nu_e oscillation explanation but does not fully exclude nu_e disappearance relevant to reactor/gallium anomalies. Reactor antineutrino anomaly significance has decreased with new flux models (Huber-Mueller re-evaluations and summation method), while BEST/gallium anomaly persists at ~5 sigma, keeping SBL motivation alive. Literature consensus is that standard thermalization is unavoidable for SBL best-fit mixing (Delta m^2~1.3 eV^2, sin^2 2theta~0.01-0.4) unless non-standard suppression (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2 or secret self-interactions) is invoked, which itself is constrained by BBN and CMB free-streaming.

Anchor points: BEST-like 1 eV 0.4 gives N_eff=4.044 Omega=22.0 excluded; reactor-like 0.09 same N_eff Omega=4.96 excluded; low-mixing 1e-3 gives N_eff=3.44 Omega=0.055 allowed; keV contrast 7100 eV 7e-11 gives Delta N_eff=0.00043 N_eff=3.044 Omega=0.033 allowed. Full scan 0.1-10 eV 3600 points (scan_DW_9bdb63.csv/.npz) finds 2597/3600 BBN-excluded and 2362/3600 overclosing, BBN-allowed max sin^2 2theta=0.00122. BBN impact plot Figure 1 bbn_vs_neff.png quantifies SM Yp=0.2468 D/H=2.443e-5 vs N_eff=4.044 Yp=0.2596 D/H=2.777e-5 (3.7 sigma in Yp), slopes dYp/dN_eff=0.0135 and dD/H/dN_eff=0.331e-5, BBN alone limits Delta N_eff<0.55 at 95%. result.summary:
Direction d-06 asked what non-standard physics would be needed to save an eV sterile neutrino (a fourth neutrino with mass ~1 eV) given cosmological limits on extra radiation. Standard cosmology excludes it; any loophole must suppress its contribution by more than a factor of three and is itself constrained.

What was established:
- The cosmological limit is N_eff (effective number of relativistic species, Standard Model predicts 3.044) = 2.99 +/- 0.17 from Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO. This implies Delta N_eff (extra radiation beyond Standard Model) < 0.28 at 95% confidence (Gaussian 1.96 sigma upper limit on observed Delta = -0.054 +/- 0.17). A fully thermalized eV sterile contributes Delta N_eff = 1.0, so it must be suppressed by factor >3.6 (1.0/0.28) to survive.
- Two anchor points computed locally with predict_sterile_nu (Dodelson-Widrow production, no lepton asymmetry): canonical BEST short-baseline best fit (m_s = 1.14 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.42, where sin^2 2theta measures mixing with active neutrinos) gives Delta N_eff = 1.0, total N_eff = 4.044, relic density Omega_s h^2 = 29.3 (244 times observed dark matter 0.12), BBN helium mass fraction Yp = 0.2596 versus observed 0.2449 +/- 0.004 and deuterium D/H = 2.78e-5 versus 2.547 +/- 0.025e-5, Delta chi^2_BBN = 23.1 versus Standard Model (threshold 3.84 at 95%), excluded at 6.2 sigma versus Planck. Low-mixing threshold point (m_s = 1.0 eV, sin^2 2theta = 0.001) gives Delta N_eff = 0.40, N_eff = 3.44, Omega_s h^2 = 0.055, Delta chi^2 = 0.62 (allowed by BBN but still above 0.28 CMB limit, 2.7 sigma tension).
- Three loophole classes identified from web_search literature leads (2024-2026 snippets, not citable): large lepton asymmetry L ~ 1e-2 (especially flavor-asymmetric with near-zero total asymmetry washed out by oscillations at MeV, evading BBN/CMB), secret neutrino self-interactions (finite-temperature suppression of active-sterile mixing), and low reheating temperature T_RH << 100 MeV (production never completes). Each can in principle reduce Delta N_eff from 1.0 to <0.28 but is independently limited by BBN Yp/D/H, CMB free-streaming, structure formation and laboratory bounds.
- Viability statement: eV 3+1 sterile neutrinos are excluded in standard cosmology; viable only with non-standard suppression that is itself constrained and requires tuned parameters.

turns.text: Continue the prior research on 'Short-baseline anomalies vs N_eff constraints'. Read the board, identify the two weakest claims, deepen them with a contrasting emulator/tool call and one new paper per weak claim, and post corrected findings before writing the report.

**Survey.** The team found 32 tools on 3 servers and 5 relevant papers, and ran 6 read-only probes.

The eV sterile neutrino interpretation of LSND (3.8 sigma) and MiniBooNE low-energy excess is in strong tension with cosmology: a fully thermalized eV sterile gives Delta N_eff ~1, excluded by Planck 2018 N_eff=2.99+/-0.17 and BBN Yp/D/H. MicroBooNE LAr data disfavors the simple nu_mu->nu_e oscillation explanation but does not fully exclude nu_e disappearance relevant to reactor/gallium anomalies. Reactor antineutrino anomaly significance has decreased with new flux models (Huber-Mueller re-evaluations and summation method), while BEST/gallium anomaly persists at ~5 sigma, keeping SBL motivation alive. Literature consensus is that standard thermalization is unavoidable for SBL best-fit mixing (Delta m^2~1.3 eV^2, sin^2 2theta~0.01-0.4) unless non-standard suppression (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2 or secret self-interactions) is invoked, which itself is constrained by BBN and CMB free-streaming.

The plan should check:
- Delta N_eff and N_eff at CMB (Planck) vs BBN.
- Primordial helium Yp and deuterium D/H shift from extra radiation.
- Sterile mass m_s and Delta m^2_41 = 1.3 eV^2 SBL best-fit.
- Mixing amplitude sin^2 2theta (appearance sin^2 2theta_mu_e vs disappearance sin^2 2theta_ee).
- Effective sterile mass m_eff_sterile = Delta N_eff * m_s and Omega_s h^2.
- Thermalization fraction / Delta N_eff vs (m_s, sin^2 2theta) grid.

**Plan.** Three lines of investigation.

1. Harden weakest claim 1: SBL anomaly status (MicroBooNE appearance exclusion vs BEST/gallium persistence and reactor flux re-evaluation) with verbatim citations and published figures. Board shows d-02/d-04 blocked on citations/figures: no .bib with verbatim quotes, no extracted figures, web_search only. Success criteria require 5 citations including arXiv:2504.16590 and 1-2 figures. This is the most cited weakness in findings f-009 to f-017 and dead ends x-03/x-07.
2. Harden weakest claim 2: non-standard loopholes (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2 and secret interactions G_X) required to suppress Delta N_eff=1.0 to <0.28 and their independent BBN/CMB constraints. Board shows d-06 blocked: no quantitative per-loophole limits, no citations, only web_search snippets. Findings claim suppression factor >3.6 needed but lack L, G_X, T_RH thresholds and BBN/CMB free-streaming bounds. Needs contrasting calculation and new papers.
3. Robustness cross-check: BBN Yp/D/H vs N_eff relation and exclusion-plane statistics with independent tool validation. Supports both weak claims with reproducible numbers: prior d-01/d-05 established slopes dYp/dN_eff=0.0135 and BBN limit Delta N_eff<0.55 but compute_statistics failed and overlay plot lacked SBL contours. Provides independent validation past standard thermalization.

The critic asked for changes:
- Tool budget exceeded: ~19 calls estimated (list/read x3 + web_search x1 + read_arxiv_chunk x5 + cite x5 + get_paper_figures x2 + describe/check/grid/predict x3) >15 limit. Consolidate web_search to 1-2 calls and batch read_arxiv_chunk/cite; drop redundant list_agent_files/list_files/read_text_file to one board check.
- Mixing definition risk: check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly is fixed to Delta m2=1.3 eV2, sin2 2theta=0.42 (disappearance). Contrasting appearance sin2 2theta_mu_e~0.01 vs disappearance sin2 2theta_ee~0.1-0.3 requires explicit conversion sin2 2theta_mu_e = sin2 2theta_ee * sin2 2theta_mumu /4 and note tool does not distinguish flavors; otherwise tension quantification is unverifiable.
- Figure extraction fragility: get_paper_figures requires arXiv HTML and often fails for 2210.10216/2201.07327. Add fallback to read_arxiv_chunk caption extraction and do not gate success on 2 figures; 1 figure with saved caption is sufficient.

**Wave 1.** Three directions run in parallel.
- Harden weakest claim 1: SBL anomaly status (MicroBooNE appearance exclusion vs BEST/gallium persistence and reactor flux re-evaluation) with verbatim citations and published figures.
- Harden weakest claim 2: non-standard loopholes (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2 and secret interactions G_X) required to suppress Delta N_eff=1.0 to <0.28 and their independent BBN/CMB constraints.
- Robustness cross-check: BBN Yp/D/H vs N_eff relation and exclusion-plane statistics with independent tool validation.

**Blocked — Harden weakest claim 2: non-standard loopholes (large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2 and secret interactions G_X) required to suppress Delta N_eff=1.0 to <0.28 and their independent BBN/CMB constraints.** Tool budget (3 calls) exhausted after contrasting emulator calls; no budget remained for read_arxiv_chunk/cite to extract verbatim quantitative limits on L, G_X, T_RH and their BBN/CMB constraints. Recorded as dead end x-08. Direction d-08 partially completed: standard thermalization quantified, loophole citations not completed due to tool budget. What was established (with emulator evidence): - BEST best-fit sterile neutrino (mass m_s=1.14 eV, Delta m^2=1.3 eV^2, mixing sin^2 2theta=0.42) fully thermalizes to Delta N_eff=1.0, giving total N_eff=4.044. This is in 6.2-sigma tension with Planck 2018 N_eff=2.99±0.17 (95% limit N_eff<3.30, Delta N_eff<0.28) and excluded by BBN at Delta chi^2=23.1 versus the Standard Model (Yp=0.2596 versus observed 0.2449±0.004; D/H=2.78e-5 versus 2.547±0.025e-5). Relic density Omega_s h^2=29.3 overcloses dark matter (observed 0.12±0.001). Evidence: check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly and predict_sterile_nu. - Mixing scan at fixed m_s=1.14 eV shows Delta N_eff=1.0 persists down to sin^2 2theta=0.01 (still BBN-excluded, Delta chi^2=23.1), falling to 0.40 at 1e-3 and 0.04 at 1e-4. Planck limit Delta N_eff<0.28 requires suppression factor >3.6 (1.0/0.28) from the canonical value, implying allowed mixing below ~5e-4, more than 20 times below SBL appearance best-fit (~0.01) and ~800 times below BEST disappearance (0.42). File: sterile_nu_grid_DW_fd1398.csv in runs/261107_174613. No figures produced. What was not done: 2-3 verbatim citations with quantitative thresholds for large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2, secret-interaction coupling G_X, and low reheating temperature T_RH, and their independent BBN/CMB free-streaming limits. Web search identified candidate papers (arXiv:1406.3208 secret interactions, arXiv:2008.06588 low T_RH, 2024-2025 lepton asymmetry) but read_arxiv_chunk and cite could not run before budget exhaustion. Corrected finding distinguishing standard exclusion from loophole viability remains incomplete.

**Completed — Robustness cross-check: BBN Yp/D/H vs N_eff relation and exclusion-plane statistics with independent tool validation.** Robustness cross-check completed for BBN Yp/D/H vs N_eff and exclusion-plane statistics. What was asked: reproduce the BBN helium and deuterium shift with extra radiation and independently validate the sterile-neutrino exclusion statistics. What came out: the relation is reproduced and SBL best-fit mixings are 7 to 313 times above the BBN-allowed maximum. BBN Yp/D/H vs N_eff (extra radiation measured as Delta N_eff, where 0 is Standard Model and 1 is one fully thermalized sterile neutrino): Standard Model (N_eff=3.044) predicts primordial helium mass fraction Yp=0.2468 and deuterium D/H x1e5=2.443; one thermalized sterile (N_eff=4.044) predicts Yp=0.2596 and D/H x1e5=2.777, which is 3.7 sigma above observed Yp=0.2449 +/-0.004. Slopes near Standard Model are dYp/dN_eff=0.0135 and dD/H5/dN_eff=0.331. BBN alone limits Delta N_eff <0.55 at 95% confidence (Delta chi-squared vs Standard Model >3.84). Files: bbn_vs_neff.png and bbn_vs_neff.pdf (Figure 3) in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_174613. 3600-point scan (sterile mass 0.1 to 10 eV, mixing sin^2 2theta 1e-4 to 0.5, Dodelson-Widrow production): 2479 of 3600 points (68.9%) are BBN-excluded at 95% and 2258 of 3600 (62.7%) overclose the universe (relic density Omega_s h^2 >0.12 vs observed 0.12). Maximum BBN-allowed mixing is sin^2 2theta=0.00134 across 0.1 to 5 eV. Independent validation via load_table_data and compute_statistics gives Delta chi-squared mean 15.10, standard deviation 10.83, range -1.15 to 23.10, median 23.10, confirming a bimodal population split between allowed and fully thermalized. N_eff mean 3.78 +/-0.38, range 3.08 to 4.04. Files: scan_DW_aa8803.csv and scan_DW_aa8803.npz in same run directory. SBL quantification (short-baseline anomalies at Delta m^2 ~1.3 eV^2): BEST gallium best fit sin^2 2theta=0.42 is 313 times above limit, reactor anomaly 0.09 is 67 times above, LSND appearance 0.01 is 7.5 times above. All three give Delta N_eff=1.0, Delta chi-squared=23.1, and overclosure Omega_s h^2 0.70 to 29.3. Only sin^2 2theta=0.001 (0.75 times limit) is allowed with Delta N_eff=0.40 and Delta chi-squared=0.62. File: sterile_nu_grid_DW_921ff8.csv. Exclusion plane reproduced as exclusion_scan_DW_aa8803.png/pdf (Figure 4) with BBN, overclosure, X-ray and Lyman-alpha limits. What ran: scan_sterile_nu_parameters (3600 points), plot_sterile_nu_bbn_impact, predict_sterile_nu_grid (6 benchmarks), predict_sterile_nu (2 points), load_table_data, compute_statistics and compute_percentiles, plot_sterile_nu_exclusion, all on local dispatch in run 261107_174613. What was not done: graphical overlay of SBL contours on the exclusion plane requires custom plotting code not available via hosted tools; quantification was done numerically instead.

**Blocked — Harden weakest claim 1: SBL anomaly status (MicroBooNE appearance exclusion vs BEST/gallium persistence and reactor flux re-evaluation) with verbatim citations and published figures.** Tool budget exhausted (3 calls remaining at user notice, then zero). Figure extraction blocked by missing HTML renderings for both target papers (dead end x-11, tc-51/52). Citation hardening blocked by quote validation failures for Planck and MicroBooNE (dead end x-12, tc-70/75) - requires read_arxiv_chunk which could not be run within budget. Only 1 of 5 required citations and 0 of 2 figures completed. Direction d-07 asked whether the eV sterile neutrino explanation for short-baseline anomalies survives cosmology and MicroBooNE. The contrasting emulator calls are complete and posted; literature hardening is partial and blocked by tool budget and figure extraction limits. What was established and posted: - BEST best-fit point (mass splitting Delta m^2 ~1.3 eV^2, mixing sin^2 2theta =0.42, sterile mass m_s ~1.14 eV, Dodelson-Widrow production) predicts extra radiation Delta N_eff =1.0 for total N_eff =4.044, where N_eff counts relativistic species at recombination. Planck 2018 measures N_eff =2.99 +/-0.17, so this is 6.2 sigma high. BBN light-element yields shift to helium mass fraction Yp =0.2596 (observed 0.2449 +/-0.004) and deuterium D/H =2.78e-5 (observed 2.547e-5 +/-0.025e-5), giving Delta chi^2 vs Standard Model =23.1, excluded at 95% (threshold 3.84). Relic density Omega_s h^2 =29.3 vastly exceeds observed dark matter 0.12 +/-0.001. Finding f-044, evidence tc-261107_1-w1-d-07-49. - Appearance mixing (sin^2 2theta_mu_e ~0.01, relevant to LSND/MiniBooNE nu_mu to nu_e) and disappearance mixing (sin^2 2theta_ee ~0.1-0.42, relevant to BEST/gallium and reactor nu_e disappearance) at the same mass both fully thermalize to Delta N_eff =1.0 with identical BBN Delta chi^2 =23.1 and overclosure (Omega_s h^2 =0.70 at 0.01, 6.98 at 0.1, 29.3 at 0.42). MicroBooNE exclusion of appearance therefore does not relieve cosmology tension for disappearance parameter space. Finding f-045, evidence tc-261107_1-w1-d-07-49 and tc-261107_1-w1-d-07-50. Grid CSV saved to /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_174613/sterile_nu_grid_DW_194dfa.csv. - One of five required verbatim citations secured in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sbl-neff/runs/261107_174613/references.bib: arXiv:2504.16590 (Ciuffoli et al., Testing the Gallium anomaly using Electron-Neutrino Scattering) with validated quote on GALLEX/SAGE/BEST deficit. Finding f-050, evidence tc-261107_1-w1-d-07-69. No figures extracted (0 of 1-2 required). What ran and what did not: All emulator calls ran locally via the sterile-neutrino server (check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly and predict_sterile_nu_grid). Web search for arXiv IDs hit DNS errors for most queries. get_paper_figures failed for both arXiv:2210.10216 and arXiv:2504.16590 due to no usable HTML rendering. cite failed for arXiv:1807.06209 and arXiv:2210.10216 because web-search snippets are not verbatim source text. What remains open: Four citations still needed (including Planck 1807.06209, MicroBooNE 2210.10216, reactor flux 2201.07327, STEREO/PROSPECT 2024) requiring read_arxiv_chunk to obtain exact quotes before retrying cite; 1-2 published figures with captions requiring PDF fallback or manual capture; reactor flux re-evaluation and STEREO/PROSPECT null quantification not yet cited.

**Critic, wave 1.** Two findings stand up to the evidence. Eight are questioned:
- "BBN Yp and D/H vs N_eff relation reproduced: SM (N_eff=3.044) gives Yp=0.2468 and D/H…" — Core Yp/D/H endpoints and BBN limit Delta N_eff<0.55 are in tc-37/tc-44/tc-45, but slopes dYp/dN_eff=0.0135 and dD/H5/dN_eff=0.331 are not present in any excerpt; they are derived values not quoted by tools.
- "3600-point DW scan (m_s 0.1-10 eV, sin^2 2theta 1e-4 to 0.5) yields 2479/3600 (68.9%)…" — tc-36 supports 2479/3600 BBN-excluded and 2258/3600 overclosing, but maximum BBN-allowed mixing sin^2 2theta_max=0.00134 across 0.1-5 eV and null at 10 eV is not in the excerpt.
- "SBL preferred regions exceed BBN-allowed maximum by large factors: BEST (sin^2…" — tc-36 and tc-41 support BEST point 0.42 with Delta N_eff=1.0, Delta chi2=23.1, Omega=29.3, but reactor 0.09 (67x), LSND 0.01 (7.5x), factors 313x, and allowed point sin^2=0.001 with Delta N_eff=0.40, Delta chi2=0.62 are not in excerpts; only one row (0.42) is shown.
- "BEST best-fit sterile neutrino (Delta m^2=1.3 eV^2, sin^2 2theta=0.42, m_s~1.14 eV)…" — tc-49 supports Delta N_eff=1.0, N_eff=4.044, Yp=0.2596, D/H=2.78e-5, Delta chi2=23.1, Omega=29.3, but Planck N_eff=2.99+/-0.17, 6.2 sigma, and Delta m^2=1.3 eV^2 are not in tool output.

The critic also noted:
- Weakest claim 1 blocked: 4 of 5 verbatim citations missing (Planck 1807.06209, MicroBooNE 2210.10216, reactor flux 2201.07327, STEREO/PROSPECT) due to quote validation failures requiring read_arxiv_chunk; 0 of 2 figures extracted due to missing HTML rendering (dead ends x-11, x-12). Emulator contrast done but literature hardening incomplete.
- Weakest claim 2 blocked: quantitative thresholds for large lepton asymmetry L~1e-2, secret interaction G_X, low reheating T_RH and their independent BBN/CMB free-streaming constraints uncited; no contrasting emulator for suppressed thermalization (dead end x-08). Standard thermalization quantified but loophole viability not distinguished.
- Robustness closed numerically but mixing definition risk remains (tool does not distinguish appearance sin^2 2theta_mu_e vs disappearance sin^2 2theta_ee) and graphical SBL overlay on exclusion plane not produced; slopes and max mixing values lack direct tool quotes.

**After wave 1.** d-07 and d-08 were blocked solely by tool budget exhaustion (3 calls remaining then zero) with emulator work complete but literature hardening incomplete; with 15 calls and 21 minutes restored the blockers are removed so both are reopened. d-09 robustness is already closed numerically and needs no further work. Two focused hardening directions replace the blocked ones, each pairing one contrasting emulator grid (appearance vs disappearance for d-07, DW vs suppressed Delta N_eff for d-08) with one new paper citation per weak claim and verbatim quote validation, fitting within the 15-call budget and posting corrected findings before report.

New directions:

- Harden weakest claim 2: non-standard loophole suppression thresholds L~1e-2, G_X, T_RH and independent BBN/CMB constraints with contrasting suppressed thermalization emulator.

No new tool calls executed in this wave: tool budget was exhausted on entry (tc-261107_1-w2-d-10-94/95/96 rejected), so citations and figure extraction could not be attempted. ABSTRACT
We present cosmological parameter results from the ﬁnal full-mission Planck measurements of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) an-
isotropies, combining information from the temperature and polarization maps and the lensing reconstruction. Compared to the 2015 results,
improved measurements of large-scale polarization allow the reionization optical depth to be measured with higher precision, leading to signiﬁ-
cant gains in the precision of other correlated parameters. Improved modelling of the small-scale polarization leads to more robust constraints on
many parameters, with residual modelling uncertainties estimated to aﬀect them only at the 0.5σ level. We ﬁnd good consistency with the standard
spatially-ﬂat 6-parameter ΛCDM cosmology having a power-law spectrum of adiabatic scalar perturbations (denoted “baseΛCDM” in this paper),
from polarization, temperature, and lensing, separately and in combination. A combined analysis gives dark matter densityΩch2 = 0.120± 0.001,
baryon density Ωbh2 = 0.0224± 0.0001, scalar spectral index ns = 0.965± 0.004, and optical depth τ = 0.054± 0.007 (in this abstract we quote
68 % conﬁdence regions on measured parameters and 95 % on upper limits). The angular acoustic scale is measured to 0 .03 % precision, with
100θ∗ = 1.0411± 0.0003. These results are only weakly dependent on the cosmological model and remain stable, with somewhat increased errors,
in many commonly considered extensions. Assuming the base- ΛCDM cosmology, the inferred (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are:
Hubble constant H0 = (67.4±0.5) km s−1Mpc−1; matter density parameterΩm = 0.315±0.007; and matter ﬂuctuation amplitudeσ8 = 0.811±0.006.
We ﬁnd no compelling evidence for extensions to the base-ΛCDM model. Combining with baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements (and
considering single-parameter extensions) we constrain the eﬀective extra relativistic degrees of freedom to beNeﬀ = 2.99±0.17, in agreement with
the Standard Model prediction Neﬀ = 3.046, and ﬁnd that the neutrino mass is tightly constrained to ∑ mν < 0.12 eV. The CMB spectra continue
to prefer higher lensing amplitudes than predicted in base ΛCDM at over 2σ, which pulls some parameters that aﬀect the lensing amplitude away
from the ΛCDM model; however, this is not supported by the lensing reconstruction or (in models that also change the background geometry)
BAO data. The joint constraint with BAO measurements on spatial curvature is consistent with a ﬂat universe,ΩK = 0.001±0.002. Also combining
with Type Ia supernovae (SNe), the dark-energy equation of state parameter is measured to be w0 =−1.03± 0.03, consistent with a cosmological
constant. We ﬁnd no evidence for deviations from a purely power-law primordial spectrum, and combining with data from BAO, BICEP2, and
Keck Array data, we place a limit on the tensor-to-scalar ratio r0.002 < 0.06. Standard big-bang nucleosynthesis predictions for the helium and
deuterium abundances for the base-ΛCDM cosmology are in excellent agreement with observations. The Planck base-ΛCDM results are in good
agreement with BAO, SNe, and some galaxy lensing observations, but in slight tension with the Dark Energy Survey’s combined-probe results
including galaxy clustering (which prefers lower ﬂuctuation amplitudes or matter density parameters), and in signiﬁcant, 3.6σ, tension with local
measurements of the Hubble constant (which prefer a higher value). Simple model extensions that can partially resolve these tensions are not
favoured by the Planck data.

1. Introduction
Since their discovery (Smoot et al. 1992), temperature anisotro-
pies in the cosmic microwave background (CMB) have become
one of the most powerful ways of studying cosmology and the
physics of the early Universe. This paper reports the ﬁnal results
on cosmological parameters from the Planck Collaboration. 1
Our ﬁrst results were presented in Planck Collaboration XVI
(2014, hereafter PCP13). These were based on temperature
(T T) power spectra and CMB lensing measurements from the
ﬁrst 15.5 months of Planck data combined with the Wilkinson
Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) polarization likelihood
at multipoles𝓁≤ 23 (Bennett et al. 2013) to constrain the reion-
ization optical depth τ. Planck Collaboration XIII (2016, here-
after PCP15) reported results from the full Planck mission (29
months of observations with the High Frequency Instrument,
HFI), with substantial improvements in the characterization of
the Planck beams and absolute calibration (resolving a di ﬀer-
ence between the absolute calibrations of WMAP and Planck).
The focus of PCP15, as in PCP13, was on temperature obser-
vations, though we reported preliminary results on the high-
multipole T E and EE polarization spectra. In addition, we
used polarization measurements at low multipoles from the Low
Frequency Instrument (LFI) to constrain the value ofτ.
Following the completion of PCP15, a concerted e ﬀort by
the Planck team was made to reduce systematics in the HFI po-
larization data at low multipoles. First results were presented
in Planck Collaboration Int. XLVI (2016), which showed evi-
dence for a lower value of the reionization optical depth than
in the 2015 results. Further improvements to the HFI polariza-
tion maps prepared for the 2018 data release are described in
Planck Collaboration III (2020). In this paper, we constrain τ
using a new low-multipole likelihood constructed from these
maps. The improvements in HFI data processing since PCP15
have very little e ﬀect on the T T, T E, and EE spectra at high
multipoles. However, this paper includes characterizations of
the temperature-to-polarization leakage and relative calibrations
of the polarization spectra enabling us to produce a combined
TT,TE,EE likelihood that is of suﬃcient ﬁdelity to be used to test
cosmological models (although with some limitations, which
will be described in detail in the main body of this paper). The
focus of this paper, therefore, is to present updated cosmological
results from Planck power spectra and CMB lensing measure-
ments using temperature and polarization.
PCP13 showed that the Planck data were remarkably con-
sistent with a spatially-ﬂat ΛCDM cosmology with purely adi-
abatic, Gaussian initial ﬂuctuations, as predicted in simple in-
ﬂationary models. We refer to this model, which can be spec-
iﬁed by six parameters, as “base” ΛCDM in this paper. Note
that in the base ΛCDM cosmology we assume a single minimal-
mass neutrino eigenstate. We investigated a grid of one- and
two-parameter extensions to the base-ΛCDM cosmology (vary-
ing, for example, the sum of neutrino masses, e ﬀective number
of relativistic degrees of freedom Neﬀ, spatial curvature ΩK, or
dark-energy equation of state w0), ﬁnding no statistically signif-
icant preference for any departure from the base model. These

The analyses reported in PCP13 and PCP15 revealed some
discrepancies (often referred to as “tensions”) with non- Planck
data in the context of ΛCDM models (e.g., distance-ladder mea-
surements of the Hubble constant and determinations of the
present-day amplitude of the ﬂuctuation spectrum), including
other CMB experiments (Story et al. 2013). As a result, it is
important to test the ﬁdelity of the Planck data as thoroughly
as possible. First, we would like to emphasize that where it
has been possible to compare data between di ﬀerent exper-
iments at the map level (therefore eliminating cosmic vari-
ance), they have been found to be consistent within the lev-
els set by instrument noise, apart from overall di ﬀerences in
absolute calibration; comparisons between WMAP and Planck
are described by Huang et al. (2018), between the Atacama
Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and Planck by Louis et al. (2014),
and between the South Pole Telescope (SPT) and Planck by
Hou et al. (2018). There have also been claims of internal in-
consistencies in the Planck T T power spectrum between fre-
quencies (Spergel et al. 2015) and between the ΛCDM param-
eters obtained from low and high multipoles (Addison et al.
2016). In addition, the Planck T T spectrum preferred more
lensing than expected in the base- ΛCDM model (quantiﬁed
by the phenomenological AL parameter deﬁned in Sect. 2.3)
at moderate statistical signiﬁcance, raising the question of
whether there are unaccounted for systematic e ﬀects lurking
within the Planck data. These issues were largely addressed in
Planck Collaboration XI (2016), PCP15, and in an associated
paper, Planck Collaboration Int. LI (2017). We revisit these is-
sues in this paper at the cosmological parameter level, using
consistency with the Planck polarization spectra as an addi-
tional check. Since 2013, we have improved the absolute cal-
ibration (ﬁxing the amplitudes of the power spectra), added
Planck polarization, full-mission Planck lensing , and produced
a new low-multipole polarization likelihood from the Planck
HFI. Nevertheless, the key parameters of the base-ΛCDM model
reported in this paper, agree to better than 1σ20132 with those de-
termined from the nominal mission temperature data in PCP13,
with the exception of τ (which is lower in the 2018 analysis by
1.1σ2013). The cosmological parameters from Planck have re-
mained remarkably stable since the ﬁrst data release in 2013.
The results from Planck are in very good agree-
ment with simple single-ﬁeld models of inﬂation
(Planck Collaboration XXII 2014; Planck Collaboration XX
2016). We have found no evidence for primordial
non-Gaussianity (Planck Collaboration XXIV 2014;
Planck Collaboration XVII 2016), setting stringent up-
per limits. Nor have we found any evidence for isocur-
vature perturbations or cosmic defects (see PCP15 and
Planck Collaboration XX 2016). Planck, together with
Bicep/Keck (BICEP2 /Keck Array and Planck Collaborations
2015) polarization measurements, set tight limits on the ampli-
tude of gravitational waves generated during inﬂation. These
results are updated in this paper and in the companion papers,
describing more comprehensive tests of inﬂationary models
(Planck Collaboration X 2020) and primordial non-Gaussianity
(Planck Collaboration IX 2020). The Planck results require
adiabatic, Gaussian initial scalar ﬂuctuations, with a red-tilted
spectrum. The upper limits on gravitational waves then require
ﬂat inﬂationary potentials, which has stimulated new devel-

Ijjas & Steinhardt 2016) have come to a very di ﬀerent con-
clusion, namely that the Planck/Bicep/Keck results require
special initial conditions and therefore disfavour inﬂation. This
controversy lies ﬁrmly in the theoretical domain (see e.g.,
Guth et al. 2014; Linde 2018), since observations of the CMB
constrain only a limited number of e-folds during inﬂation, not
the initial conditions. Post Planck, inﬂation remains a viable
and attractive mechanism for accounting for the structure that
we see in the Universe.
The layout of this paper is as follows. Section 2 de-
scribes changes to our theoretical modelling since PCP15
and summarizes the likelihoods used in this paper. More
comprehensive descriptions of the power-spectrum likelihoods
are given in Planck Collaboration V (2020), while the 2018
Planck CMB lensing likelihood is described in detail in
Planck Collaboration VIII (2020). Section 3 discusses the pa-
rameters of the base- ΛCDM model, comparing parameters de-
rived from the Planck T T, T E, and EE power spectra. Our best
estimates of the base- ΛCDM cosmological parameters are de-
rived from the full Planck TT,TE,EE likelihood combined with
Planck CMB lensing and an HFI-based low-multipole polariza-
tion likelihood to constrain τ. We compare the Planck T E and
EE spectra with power spectra measured from recent ground-
based experiments in Sect. 4.
The Planck base-ΛCDM cosmology is compared with ex-
ternal data sets in Sect. 5. CMB power spectrum measurements
suﬀer from a “geometric degeneracy” (see Efstathiou & Bond
1999) which limits their ability to constrain certain extensions to
the base cosmology (for example, allowing ΩK or w0 to vary).
Planck lensing measurements partially break the geometric de-
generacy, but it is broken very e ﬀectively with the addition of
baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from galaxy
surveys. As in PCP13 and PCP15 we use BAO measurements as
the primary external data set to combine with Planck. We adopt
this approach for two reasons. Firstly, BAO-scale determinations
are relatively simple geometric measurements, with little scope
for bias from systematic errors. Secondly, the primary purpose
of this paper is to present and emphasize the Planck results. We
therefore make minimal use of external data sets in reporting
our main results, rather than combining with many diﬀerent data

We present a search for eV-scale sterile neutrino oscillations in the MicroBooNE liquid argon
detector, simultaneously considering all possible appearance and disappearance eﬀects within the
3 + 1 active-to-sterile neutrino oscillation framework. We analyze the neutrino candidate events for
the recent measurements of charged-current νe and νµ interactions in the MicroBooNE detector,
using data corresponding to an exposure of 6.37×1020 protons on target from the Fermilab booster
neutrino beam. We observe no evidence of light sterile neutrino oscillations and derive exclusion
contours at the 95% conﬁdence level in the plane of the mass-squared splitting ∆m2
41 and the sterile
neutrino mixing angles θµe andθee, excluding part of the parameter space allowed by experimental
anomalies. Cancellation of νe appearance andνe disappearance eﬀects due to the full 3+1 treatment
of the analysis leads to a degeneracy when determining the oscillation parameters, which is discussed
in this paper and will be addressed by future analyses.
The discoveries of solar [1] and atmospheric neutrino

In this Letter, we present a new analysis testing the
sterile neutrino hypothesis in a full 3 + 1 oscillation
framework with detailed event-level information. We
use the data set from the MicroBooNE inclusive νe
CC measurement [41], and compare the results to
the parameter space allowed by the LSND, gallium
(including BEST), and Neutrino-4 anomalies. We
simultaneously consider short-baseline sterile-neutrino-
induced νe appearance and νe disappearance. This
treatment can lead to cancellations that result in a
degeneracy when determining the oscillation parameters,
which we will introduce in more detail in this paper.
The MicroBooNE detector [43] is a 10.4 m long, 2.6 m
wide, and 2.3 m tall LArTPC, located on-axis of the
BNB at Fermilab. It consists of about 85 metric tons
of liquid argon in the TPC active volume for ionization
charge detection along with an array of photomultiplier
tubes [55] for scintillation light detection. It sits at a
distance of 468.5 m from the target of the BNB, which
uses protons with a kinetic energy of 8 GeV impinging on
the target, producing secondary hadrons. The hadrons
are mostly pions or kaons that decay in ﬂight, producing
a neutrino beam through their decay. The MicroBooNE
BNB data set was collected entirely in neutrino mode
and consists of a very pure νµ beam with a small ¯ νµ
contamination and a νe contamination of < 1%.
We perform a full 3 + 1 (4 ν) neutrino oscillation
analysis, capitalizing on the seven channels of νe
and νµ selections and their statistical and systematic
uncertainties from the MicroBooNE inclusive νe low-
energy excess search [41]. The analysis uses the BNB
Runs 1–3 data set with an exposure of 6.369 ×1020
protons on target (POT). In addition to the standard
Monte Carlo (MC) samples for intrinsicνe andνµ events
in the BNB, a dedicated νµ → νe oscillation sample
was generated to appropriately take into account the
ﬂux and cross-section systematic uncertainties related to
the νe appearance events. The seven channels comprise
fully contained (FC) and partially contained (PC)νe CC
processes, FC and PC νµ CC processes without ﬁnal-
state π0 mesons, FC and PC νµ CC processes with
ﬁnal-state π0 mesons, and a NC channel with ﬁnal-
state π0 mesons. The fully contained events are deﬁned
as those that have all reconstructed TPC activity (i.e.,
charge depositions) within a ﬁducial volume 3 cm from
the TPC boundaries. Because there are νµ and νe
components in the BNB ﬂux, the νe appearance (from
νµ), νe disappearance, and νµ disappearance oscillation
eﬀects in the 3 + 1 framework are simultaneously applied
to the predicted signal and background events in all
seven channels in the oscillation ﬁt. The νµ appearance
eﬀect is neglected because of the very low fraction of
intrinsic νe in the BNB ﬂux. This strategy takes full
advantage of the statistics of the selected νe and νµ
events in the FC and PC channels, and at the same time
maintains the capability to apply data constraints across
channels through a joint ﬁt to the seven channels, thereby
reducing the systematic uncertainty in the oscillation
analysis. The neutrino energy reconstruction primarily
follows a calorimetric method with an energy resolution
of approximately 10–15% and a bias of 5–10% for CC
events [41]. In the reconstruction of NC events, we
use this method to estimate the energy transfer with
an invisible outgoing neutrino. The reconstruction of
visible energy for the NC events in this analysis has a
similar bias and energy resolution to the neutrino energy
reconstruction of CC events.

Testing the Gallium anomaly using Electron-Neutrino Scattering
Emilio Ciuffoli∗a, Jarah Evslin †a,b, Ruixuan Gao c, Haixing Lin c, and Jian Tang ‡c
aInstitute of Modern Physics, NanChangLu 509, Lanzhou 730000, China

Abstract
The Gallium anomaly is an unexplained deficit in the neutrinos observed during the calibration
of GALLEX and SAGE using a 51Cr radioactive source and recently confirmed by BEST. The
possible explanations for this deficit include an overestimation of the neutrino absorption cross
section in Ga, an incorrect measurement of the source activity or the existence of sterile neutri-
nos. However, as this deficit has only been observed in Ga detectors, it has not been possible
to distinguish among various proposals. Therefore, we propose an experiment using the same
radioactive source but with a different detection method, electron-neutrino scattering. We dis-
cuss potential locations for such an experiment, estimating the main backgrounds and expected
event rates, considering various target masses and source positions. Even if the anomaly does
not result from the detection method, such an experiment can provide an independent determi-
nation of the branching ratio of the 51Cr decay by using the spectral information or observing
the scattering angle. It is also sensitive to an eventual baseline dependence of the anomaly, as
is predicted in sterile neutrino models.
1 Introduction
The GALLEX [1] and SAGE [2] experiments began operations in the late 1980s, continuing up to
the beginning of the following century. Their goal was to study solar neutrinos using a Gallium-
based detector, observing νe via the reaction
71Ga +νe→ 71Ge +e−. (1)
The main advantage of such a method is the very low energy threshold of (1), namely 234 keV,
which allowed the experiments to study neutrinos from the low-energy pp chain.
Radioactive sources were used to calibrate the detectors, most notably 51Cr1, which primarily
decays via electron capture
51Cr→ 51V +νe. (2)

The neutrino emitted is monoenergetic: in ∼ 90% if the cases its energy is Eν = Eν,2∼750 keV.
In about 10% of the cases, we have Eν =Eν,1∼430 keV and a 320 keV γ is emitted as well
51Cr→ 51V +νe +γ. (3)
During the calibration of the GALLEX and SAGE detectors, only about 80% of the expected
neutrino flux was observed. More recently, in 2022, this anomalous deficit was confirmed by the
BEST experiment [3] (see also Ref. [4] for a comprehensive review of the experimental results on
the Gallium anomaly). Currently the measured deficit, expressed as the ratio between the observed
rate and the expected one, is R =Nobs/Nexp = 0.803± 0.035 [5].
Many explanations for this deficit have been proposed. However, they are all in tension with
other experimental results, require new physics, or both (see [5] for a review). We can roughly
divide these proposed explanations into three categories: those involving the neutrino production,
detection or propagation.
The source of the anomaly could, for example, be an error in the estimation of the source
activity. The measurements are performed by detecting the γ’s emitted in ∼10% of the cases: an
error in the branching ratio (BR) for those decays would lead to an overestimation of the source
activity, explaining the anomaly. On the other hand, these branching ratios have already been
measured by several collaborations [6, 7, 8, 9], with precisions of the order of 10 −4.
Another possible class of explanations involves some errors in the estimation of the detection
rate and/or efficiency. For example, the cross-section for the reaction (1) may be underestimated,
or there may be an error in the radiochemical extraction of 71Ge from the detector, which is used
to estimate the total number of neutrinos detected. Recently, however, Ref. [10] has compared the
solar neutrino fluxes measured by the Gallium experiments with the ones measured by Borexino,
finding a substantial agreement between the two datasets. If the explanation of the anomaly relies
on the detection method, one would expect that the same deficit should apply to the measurement
of the solar neutrinos as well, but this does not appear to be the case.
A third class of explanations involves the propagation process, the most famous of which is
sterile neutrinos. This explanation gained some popularity a few years ago when it seemed possible
to simultaneously explain several neutrino anomalies (although a ”pragmatic” approach would be
needed [11], since the sterile neutrinos would not be able to explain the low-energy excess seen at
MiniBooNE) with just a single flavor of sterile neutrinos.
The hopes for a simple explanation, however, were soon quashed. First of all, the region of
the parameter space that could explain the Gallium anomaly is quite strongly excluded by short
baseline experiments, which failed to see signs of sterile neutrinos [12]. Moreover, it became clear
recently that the reactor anomaly was due to an error in the theoretical prediction of the neutrino
flux; even if the origin of the shape distortion at around 5 MeV is still unclear, it cannot be due
to the presence of sterile neutrinos. Finally, in the νµ → νe sector, the low-E neutrino excess
cannot be explained by oscillations alone (with or without sterile neutrinos), and the search for
new systematics that can justify the so-called excess has not produced any results yet.
It should also be noted that the relevant bounds on the mixing parameters that would exclude
the sterile neutrino explanation are obtained using ¯νe, while the Gallium anomaly was measured in
the neutrino sector. Even though it’s true that a CP-violating phase could introduce a difference
between the oscillation probability in the neutrino and antineutrino sector, such a difference cannot
be present in the survival probability, namely the oscillation probability for ¯ νe→ ¯νe must be the
same as for νe→νe, while the probability for ¯νµ→ ¯νe could be different from the one for νµ→νe.
Since in the Gallium anomaly we are observing the survival probability, i.e. the former, if sterile

neutrinos are the cause of the Gallium anomaly, CP violation would not be sufficient to explain
the tension with the short baseline experiments, CPT must be broken as well [13].
This is why, recently, the focus of the neutrino community shifted: instead of attempting to find
a global explanation for all the anomalies, we should try first to solve ”locally” the inconsistencies
in each channel separately, looking for an explanation for the contradictory results [14]. This,
however, requires new experimental data, which is the main motivation for our work.
We propose a test of the Gallium anomaly, still using 51Cr as a source but detecting the
neutrinos via electron-neutrino scattering, rather than neutrino capture. If the Gallium anomaly
persists without Gallium, we can exclude any explanation involving the detector. This is similar to
the ill-fated SOX experiment [15], which was proposed and then abandoned due to issues with the
delivery of the 144Ce radioactive source. For this project, however, we will need only 51Cr, which
has already been used successfully in several experiments, including GALLEX, SAGE and BEST.
A similar setup has also been proposed to study the neutrino anapole moment [16].
The main objective of this endeavor would be to measure the total neutrino flux. This would
be sufficient prove or exclude any explanations involving the detection process. A secondary and
more challenging goal would be to directly measure the BR of the 51Cr decay, which would allow
us also to test the conjecture that the anomaly is caused by the calibration of the source. The
BR would be determined by looking at the energy spectrum of the recoiled electron or, if we use
Cherenkov light, by reconstructing the scattering angle which, along with the recoil energy, would
allow us to reconstruct the neutrino energy. The requirements that must be satisfied to carry out
this measurement, however, are much steeper than the ones needed to simply confirm or deny the
presence of the anomaly. The precision that can be achieved measuring the BR using electron-
neutrino scattering is considerably worse than that obtained in the previously cited works. We
feel that this is nonetheless of interest because an error in the BR is often mentioned as possible
explanation of the anomaly, and this kind of measurement would provide an independent test of
this hypothesis. Finally, using a liquid scintillator it would also be possible to obtain information
on the spatial distribution of the events, which would allow us to see an eventual dependence of
the anomaly on the baseline. If observed, such an effect would be a strong hint in favor of sterile
neutrinos.
This work is organized as follows: in Sec. 2 we will describe how one may use electron-neutrino
scattering to test Gallium anomaly. In Sec. 3 we will consider possible locations where such an ex-
periment may be performed, computing the expected number of events and the main backgrounds.
In Sec. 4 we will show how it would be possible to measure the BR of 51Cr decay using such an
experiment, discussing the requirements needed to carry out such a measurement. In Sec. 5 we will
compute the region of the parameter space that can be tested if the anomaly is caused by sterile
neutrinos. Finally, in Sec. 6, we will summarize our results.
2 Electron-Neutrino Scattering
2.1 Cross Section
51Cr decays via electron capture, which means that a monoenergetic neutrino will be emitted. In
the majority of the cases ( ∼ 90%), the neutrino will be the only particle emitted, with energy
Eν,2 = 750 keV. In a fraction of the decays ( pBR∼ 10%), a 320 keV γ will be emitted as well,
lowering the neutrino energy to Eν,1 = 430 keV. This decay mode is extremely important because
the activity of the source is measured by detecting the γ’s, which means that even a small error in
the BR could significantly change the number of detections and so potentially explain the anomaly.
